subject: AI & Agents
title: ChatGPT: AI Goes Mainstream
description: A micro-lesson that makes ChatGPT: AI Goes Mainstream usable.

hook.text: November 30, 2022. OpenAI launches ChatGPT. It reaches 100 million users in two months.

buildup.text: ChatGPT combined GPT-3.5 with RLHF to create an AI that felt natural to talk to.

discovery.text: For the first time, non-technical people experienced powerful AI firsthand through conversation.

twist.text: Schools panicked. Companies scrambled. Competitors raced to catch up. Nothing was the same after.

climax.text: ChatGPT didn't invent the technology. It made it accessible. That was the real breakthrough.

punchline.text: The revolution wasn't the model. It was the interface.

quiz.question: What made ChatGPT a mainstream breakthrough?
options: It made powerful AI accessible through a simple conversational interface
It was the first language model ever built
It could only be used by researchers

details.summary: ChatGPT launched in November 2022 and reached 100 million users in two months, making AI accessible to the general public. It transformed how people interact with and think about artificial intelligence.
details.whyItMatters: ChatGPT brought AI into everyday life more than any prior technology. Its accessible conversational interface made millions of people direct users of advanced AI for the first time.
takeaways: ChatGPT reached 100 million users in just two months
It made conversational AI accessible to non-technical users
The launch triggered massive AI investment and public debate

faq.question: What made ChatGPT so much more popular than earlier chatbots?
faq.answer: ChatGPT combined powerful language understanding with a simple chat interface. It could write essays, code, poems, and answer complex questions in a way that felt natural and immediately useful.

faq.question: How has ChatGPT changed the AI industry?
faq.answer: It triggered billions in AI investment, launched an AI startup boom, pushed competitors to release their own models, and started global conversations about AI regulation, copyright, and education.
